en: The Lord said, "You did not labor for it
or make it grow. It came up in a night
and died in a night, yet you pitied this plant.
Should I not pity Nineveh, that great city,
with more than 120,000 people who can't tell right from left,
and many animals as well?
How could I not care for them?"
The people of Nineveh, whom God cares for,
Jonah doesn't care about at all.
But he cares enormously about his own plant,
because losing it costs him.
God is dealing with that pride.
God cares so much for those souls,

text:
그 사람의 영혼보다
자기 박넝쿨을 더 아끼는 삶
en: yet here is a life that cares more for its plant than for their souls:
that's pride. That's what pride looks like.

text:
교만은 하나님의 관심하고
전혀 *다른* 데 관심이 있는 거예요
en: Pride cares about something completely different from what God cares about.

text:
그래서 하나님의 *슬픔*이
자신의 슬픔이 되지 않습니다
en: So God's sorrow never becomes your sorrow,

text:
하나님의 미움이
자기의 미움이 되지 않는 거예요
en: and what God hates, you don't hate.
And your cynicism toward others keeps growing.
"Pastor, I'm barely getting by as it is.

text:
무슨 다른 사람에게 내가
*에너지*를 쓸 수 있겠습니까?"
en: How could I spend energy on anyone else?"
Pride is the sin of judging,

text:
그 판단의 죄는 늘
*나한테* 관심이 있는 거예요
en: and that sin is always about me.
What God cares about and what I care about are worlds apart.
